name: Won deal to cashwerk draft invoice, project and Slack handover

parameters.content:
## How it works
When a deal is marked as won in cashwerk, this workflow does the paperwork that normally follows by hand: it reads the deal with its positions, turns those positions into a draft invoice, opens the project, and posts the handover in Slack.

The deal's line items carry over one by one with description, quantity, unit and unit price. A deal line holds no tax rate, so the rate from **Billing Rules** is applied to every position. Above a net value you choose, a deposit percentage is billed as a single position instead of the full list; below it, every position goes on the invoice. A deal with no positions falls back to its deal value.

Nothing reaches the customer. The invoice stays a draft in cashwerk for someone to check and release.

## Setup steps
1. Install the community node **n8n-nodes-cashwerk** (Settings - Community nodes).
2. In cashwerk open **Settings - API Platform**, create an API key, and add it as a **cashwerk API** credential on all five cashwerk nodes: the trigger, *Get Deal*, both invoice nodes and *Create Project*.
3. Open **Billing Rules** and set the tax rate, the payment term in days, the deposit percentage and the net value above which a deposit is billed.
4. Put your Slack credential and channel on *Notify Sales*.
5. Run it once on a test deal and read the draft before you activate it.

## Limits
- Positions are copied without discounts: a per-line discount on the deal does not carry over.
- The first contact on the deal becomes the invoice recipient; a deal without a contact is skipped.
- **Only Once Per Deal** keeps its own history, so replaying a deal on purpose means clearing that history on the node.

## Trigger and guards
The trigger fires on every deal update, so the first check keeps only the ones that were just won. **Only Once Per Deal** then drops a deal it has already handled, which is what stops a second update from invoicing twice.

## Read the deal and the rules
*Get Deal* loads the deal with its contacts and its positions - the webhook body carries neither. **Billing Rules** is the one node to edit: tax rate, payment term, deposit percentage, and the net value above which a deposit is billed.

## Decide what to bill
A deal with no contact is skipped: an invoice needs a recipient. *Build Invoice* then maps the deal positions onto invoice positions, casts the decimal strings to numbers, applies the tax rate and works out the due date.

## Write it back and hand over
One of the two invoice nodes runs, never both. Both write a **draft**. The project is created from the same deal afterwards, and Slack gets the figures so sales can see what happened without opening cashwerk.

parameters.text:
=:handshake: *Deal won - {{ $('Build Invoice').item.json.summary.dealTitle }}*
{{ $('Build Invoice').item.json.isDeposit ? "Deposit invoice" : "Invoice" }} drafted: {{ $('Build Invoice').item.json.summary.positions }} position(s), {{ $('Build Invoice').item.json.summary.netBilled.toFixed(2) }} {{ $('Build Invoice').item.json.summary.currency }} net
Project opened. Both are drafts - nothing was sent.
